name: Maoism–Third Worldism
summary: Maoism–Third Worldism combines Marxism-Leninism-Maoism with a dependency-theory view that the First World is a parasitic exploiter bloc whose workers form a labor aristocracy bought off with surplus extracted from the Third World. It holds that the real revolutionary proletariat lies in Asia, Africa and Latin America and that global people's war by oppressed nations is the path to communism, with the First World's role being mainly to be defeated or to repay its debt.
scope: Maoism-Third Worldism as the defining sources (MIM(Prisons) accounts s1, s2) describe it: the current holding that the First World working class is a labor aristocracy rather than part of the exploited proletariat, and that the Third World's peoples carry world revolution. They date the name to the 2007 Sunrise Statement, which declared 'Maoism Third-Worldism' a new stage beyond the Maoist Internationalist Movement's (MIM) line, and trace its splits (Leading Light Communism, RAIM). The text they tie to it is J. Sakai's Settlers. MIM(Prisons) rejects the label for MIM Thought, so MIM's own texts count only where a defining source ties them. Excludes ordinary Marxism-Leninism-Maoism that treats First World workers as exploited, and non-Marxist Third Worldism.
